videos.title: Why the Butterfly Tastes With Its Feet #Shorts

clipCandidates.momentLabel: She is reading the leaf the way you read a label at the grocery store
clipCandidates.why: Core metaphor — the grocery store analogy makes the abstract concept instantly relatable. Most memorable line in the script.
clipCandidates.hookRewrite: Why a butterfly reads leaves like grocery labels

clipCandidates.momentLabel: When a butterfly lands on a leaf, it is not resting, it is tasting
clipCandidates.why: Core reveal — flips the assumption that landing = resting. The surprise is immediate and visual.
clipCandidates.hookRewrite: Why a butterfly landing is actually tasting

videos.title: Why the Meerkat Eats Scorpions Like Snacks #Shorts

clipCandidates.momentLabel: They are not just immune, they are trained — adults pass down the technique
clipCandidates.why: Paradox payoff — immunity is genetic but the technique is cultural. The idea of animal culture is surprising and memorable.
clipCandidates.hookRewrite: Why meerkats teach their babies to hunt scorpions

clipCandidates.momentLabel: Adult catches scorpion, bites off stinger, hands rest to pup to practice
clipCandidates.why: Teaching moment — the step-by-step process is concrete and visual. A 10-week-old pup taking down a scorpion is a strong image.
clipCandidates.hookRewrite: How a meerkat mom teaches pups to kill scorpions

videos.title: Why the Seal Follows Fish Trails We Can't See #Shorts

clipCandidates.momentLabel: Blind seals still hunt successfully because they do not need their eyes
clipCandidates.why: Core reveal — blindness doesn't stop hunting. The whiskers alone are enough. Flips expectations about what senses matter underwater.
clipCandidates.hookRewrite: Why blind seals can still hunt fish

clipCandidates.momentLabel: It is sonar you can touch
clipCandidates.why: Closing metaphor — distills the entire concept into 6 words. Memorable and shareable.
clipCandidates.hookRewrite: Why a seal has sonar you can touch

videos.title: Why the Hawk Sees Invisible Trails to Its Prey #Shorts

clipCandidates.momentLabel: Urine trails glow like neon arrows pointing straight down to dinner
clipCandidates.why: Core visual — the neon arrow metaphor makes UV vision tangible. A vole's hiding is futile against a glowing highway.
clipCandidates.hookRewrite: Why a hawk sees glowing trails to hidden prey

clipCandidates.momentLabel: Reading a map written in light you cannot even imagine
clipCandidates.why: Closing — the 4-vs-3 receptor comparison plus the 'map written in light' metaphor is the emotional payoff.
clipCandidates.hookRewrite: Why hawks see colors you will never see

videos.title: Why the Bear Can Smell Food From 20 Miles Away #Shorts

comments.author: @donhansen1751
comments.replyText: Thank you! It really is incredible. That smelling surface being 100 times larger than ours is hard to even imagine. A bear does not just smell food nearby — it reads a map of direction, distance, and what kind of food is waiting, all from molecules on the wind. Glad you enjoyed it!

clipCandidates.momentLabel: A bear does not just smell what is nearby, a bear smells a map
clipCandidates.why: Core reveal — the 'map' metaphor elevates from simple smell to spatial intelligence. Most surprising claim.
clipCandidates.hookRewrite: Why a bear doesn't just smell — it sees a map

clipCandidates.momentLabel: A sealed cooler will not fool one, a car trunk will not fool one
clipCandidates.why: Practical implication — relatable to campers. The ranger quote lands the point.
clipCandidates.hookRewrite: Why no cooler or car trunk can hide food from a bear
